reptimorphPageTitle: Reptimorph - Reptile marketplace for breeders and individuals
reptimorphPageInfo1Text: Reptimorph is a European marketplace connecting professional breeders and individuals for the sale of reptiles, fish and terrarium equipment.
reptimorphPageInfo1Item1: Next.js on the front for SSR rendering and optimal SEO performance
reptimorphPageInfo1Item2: NestJS on the back for a modular architecture and robust data control
reptimorphPageInfo1Item3: PostgreSQL with Prisma as ORM, hosted on Railway
reptimorphPageInfo1Item4: Multilingual FR / EN with Lingui and locale management via Next.js App Router
reptimorphPageInfo2Text: The core of Reptimorph is its listing marketplace. Sellers publish their animals with photos (Cloudinary), species, genetic morphs, location (MapBox) and price.
reptimorphPageInfo2Item1: Infinite scroll with cursor-based pagination on the API for optimal performance
reptimorphPageInfo2Item2: Dynamic filters by taxon (species), genetic morphs, location and price
reptimorphPageInfo2Item3: Listing boost system for better visibility
reptimorphPageInfo2Item5: Genetic morph management: database of possible combinations per species
reptimorphPageInfo3Text: Transactions are secured via Stripe. Each seller creates their Stripe Connect account directly from their dashboard to receive payments.
reptimorphPageInfo3Item1: Stripe Connect for seller account management and automatic transfers
reptimorphPageInfo3Item2: Stripe webhooks for real-time order status synchronisation
reptimorphPageInfo3Item4: Repticoins: internal currency for boosts and additional services
reptimorphPageInfo4Text: Reptimorph goes beyond the marketplace with a real community space for reptile enthusiasts.
reptimorphPageInfo4Item1: Real-time private messaging between buyers and sellers via Socket.io
reptimorphPageInfo4Item2: Community forum with threads and replies
reptimorphPageInfo4Item3: Events: creation and participation in reptile events
reptimorphPageInfo4Item4: Follow, favourites, reviews and reporting system
reptimorphPageInfo4Item5: OAuth authentication (Google) + two-factor authentication (2FA) for security
reptimorphPageInfo4Item6: Integrated AI assistant to help users
flunPageTitle: Flun - AI-powered mobile story creation app
flunPageInfo1Text: Flun is an iOS and Android mobile app for creating personalised children's stories with AI-generated illustrations. Text is produced by GPT-4o-mini and illustrations by Replicate.
flunPageInfo1Item1: React Native / Expo for shared iOS & Android code
flunPageInfo1Item2: NestJS on the back for a robust modular architecture
flunPageInfo1Item5: Light / dark theme with night mode
flunPageInfo2Text: The user describes their story, chooses an illustration style, age group, language and number of pages. The AI then generates the text and a unique illustration per page.
flunPageInfo2Item1: Text generation via OpenAI GPT-4o-mini with a professional system prompt
flunPageInfo2Item2: Page-by-page illustrations via Replicate (AI image models)
flunPageInfo2Item3: Visual consistency of characters guaranteed across all pages
flunPageInfo2Item4: Generation queue to handle simultaneous requests
flunPageInfo2Item5: StoryCoins system: internal currency to create stories
flunPageInfo3Text: Users can create their own reusable characters across multiple stories. Each character is precisely described to guarantee visual consistency between illustrations.
flunPageInfo3Item1: Create human or animal characters with detailed appearance
flunPageInfo3Item2: Attributes: skin colour, hair, eyes, gender, outfit, accessories
flunPageInfo3Item3: Characters are injected into the generation prompt for each page
flunPageInfo4Text: Flun is monetised through a subscription and StoryCoins system, managed by native iOS and Android in-app purchases.
flunPageInfo4Item1: Premium subscriptions via IAP (In-App Purchase) iOS & Android
flunPageInfo4Item2: Server-side receipt verification to secure transactions
flunPageInfo4Item3: StoryCoins: credits for creating stories outside of a subscription
flunPageInfo4Item4: Stripe as a complement for web payments
flunPageInfo5Text: Users can share their stories with others and create groups for shared experiences.
flunPageInfo5Item1: Share public stories and browse shared stories
flunPageInfo5Item2: Groups: create or join groups to share stories
flunPageInfo5Item3: Group invitations via push notifications (Expo Notifications)
myAgendaPageInfo1Text: This site allows users to easily manage their daily routine and organise their events.
myAgendaPageInfo1Item1: When creating an account, a 'user' is saved in the database containing an email, password, username and image.
myAgendaPageInfo1Item2: On login, a token is generated with JWT to verify the user's identity.
myAgendaPageInfo2Text: After logging in, the user is redirected to their Dashboard.
myAgendaPageInfo2Item2: All events created by the user are fetched from the database using their id
myAgendaPageInfo3Text: The user can create, edit or delete an event from multiple tabs.
myAgendaPageInfo3Item1: Create, delete or edit an 'event' in the database
myAgendaPageInfo4Text: Once created, events are available across multiple tabs.
myAgendaPageInfo5Text: Days of the current month are clickable and scroll to the corresponding section. The event date is compared to decide whether to display it or not.

pageInfoEldenLore: This site about the Elden Ring universe allows users to create an account, then log in to create articles where they can share their knowledge about a boss, weapon, item, or character encountered in the game.
pageInfoEldenLore2: The articles are present on the homepage, and the search bar moves to the header when scrolling so that the user can perform searches at any time. They can also click on the icon next to the section title to filter articles by category.
pageInfoEldenLore3: Creating an account requires a username, a password, and an image from the user. This information is then stored in a 'users' table, which will be used to authenticate the user when logging in.
pageInfoEldenLore4: Once logged in, the user will have the ability to create articles that will be available on the homepage. They can then edit or delete them by clicking on the corresponding icons on their articles.
pageInfoEldenLore5: By clicking on an article, we are redirected to a page dedicated to it, where users who have created an account can comment on each other's articles.
pageInfoEldenLore6: The site also contains a 'Lore' section that explains the context in which the game's story takes place.
pageInfoEldenLore7: Creating and editing an article is done in the same way: a form to fill out and a real-time preview of the article. If the information is valid, the article is successfully added or edited; otherwise, an error message is displayed.
pageInfoTenCents: 10 Cents is an online gambling application in the form of a lottery, where users can play coins together.
tenCentsSub: When opening the application, the user has two choices: create an account or log in.
tenCentsSub2: To create an account, the user can choose between using an email or a phone number.
tenCentsSub3: To start, we send a six-digit code to verify their identity. To do this, a 'verifEmail' object is created; this object has its own ID and contains the email and the code sent.
tenCentsSub4: Next, we compare the email provided in the previous step and the code entered by the user with the corresponding 'verifEmail' object. If the code matches, we proceed to the next step; otherwise, a message indicates an error.
tenCentsSub5: The user then chooses a password, which must meet the required conditions, then the user must confirm their password. Once the password is validated, a 'user' is created.
tenCentsSub6: Finally, the user chooses a username and a profile picture. The picture is converted to 'webp' format and resized using a middleware and 'multer'. If the username and picture are correctly provided and uploaded, a 'profile' object is created.
tenCentsSub7: Account creation complete! The database now contains a 'user' object whose ID corresponds to the 'ID' property of the 'profile'. The user can now begin their experience on 10 Cents!
tenCentsLog: As with account creation, the user can choose an email or a phone number to log in.
tenCentsLog2: Here, we compare the email and password provided with the 'users' registered in the database. If the data matches, they can access their account; otherwise, an error message pop.
tenCentsLog3: In case of 'forgot password', we send a email with 'sendGrid'. We create a 'PasswordReset' object containing the token and the email. Then, the token is added to the link to the reset page for the next step.
tenCentsPages: Home page, containing the user's information, their number of tokens, and a history section containing their ongoing games, purchases, and results of previous games.
tenCentsPages2: Social media page, containing links to our Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook accounts, where they can share their experience.
tenCentsPages3: Offers page, containing our token offers as well as premium subscription offers.
tenCentsPages4: Settings page, where the user can choose a language and a theme, manage notification settings, change their username and profile picture, view subscription information and access the 'log out' or 'delete my account' functions.
tenCentsPages5: Games page, containing our different games and their information, number of participants, start date, and availability. (More details in the 'user experience' section).
tenCentsGame: To start, the user needs tokens. Go to the offers page, where the user will choose the offer of 10 tokens and a premium subscription. This will modify the profile's properties.
tenCentsGame2: The user's information is updated accordingly, as well as their history. For each purchase, a 'history' object is created.
tenCentsGame3: Here, the user sign up for '1 VS 10'. His account is debited 1 token, and the 'play' button is no longer clickable. At the same time, a 'game' is created containing an ID and a 'participants' property in which the user's ID is added.
tenCentsGame4: Once the 'registerToGame' property changes to 'true', a reminder is added to the user's history. It will remain until 'registerToGame' changes to 'false' (end of the game).
tenCentsGame5: When the game start, a function will randomly select a winner among the 'participants' registered in each 'game' present in the database. The displayed winner is the one from the game in which the user's ID is listed. If they win, their number of tokens will increase based on the number of participants.
tenCentsGame6: The player won, so he get his token back, a 'history' object was created containing the result 'Winner' or 'Loser', the game name, the date, and the number of tokens won.
